sections.html:
Daviess County is western Kentucky's river-city market, anchored by Owensboro on the Ohio River. It covers 477 square miles, 18 of them water. The north is mostly level river land, while the south rolls into hills and valleys. The county had 103,312 residents in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate of 104,898 is 1.5 percent higher.

There are 45,155 housing units across 41,639 households, and 68.1 percent of households own, so close to a third rent. A typical home is valued at $199,900 and typical rent is $918 a month. Typical monthly owner cost is $1,387 with a mortgage and $512 without. The county issued 253 building permits in 2025, which keeps some new inventory in the mix.

sections.h2: Who sends and collects the bill
sections.html:
Billing and collection both sit with the Sheriff's Office tax division, found at 212 St. Ann Street, Room 103, in Owensboro. The counter answers questions at 270-685-6133 on weekdays until 4:30 and closes on major holidays.

Bills are mailed during the first week of November. Even with a lender paying from escrow, you may get a bill, because servicers sometimes plan to pay without asking the sheriff to hold a copy. If you expect a bill and see none, allow a couple of days for postal delays, then look the parcel up on the sheriff's website, since the mailing address on file may be wrong. Call or email the tax counter with the parcel numbers to correct an address. Property inside Owensboro also owes city tax through the City of Owensboro Tax Office at 270-687-8537.

In August 2025 the Fiscal Court adopted the compensating rate for real property, which moved the county's figure from 12.9 cents to 12.2 cents per $100 of assessed value. Tangible personal property stayed at 13.8 cents, and motor vehicles and watercraft at 17 cents.

The county's share is only part of the picture. Schools and other taxing bodies add theirs, so the full rate on a parcel runs above 12.2 cents. Pull a parcel-level bill from the tax counter or the sheriff's website before quoting a buyer the carrying cost.

One state-approved calendar repeats yearly. Pay in the first window to save 2 percent, which is worth doing if you can. Every later window costs more.

Under KRS 134.119, a mailed payment with a U.S. Postal Service postmark inside the window is on time. A returned check costs $25, and the bill goes back to unpaid.

Three channels work. Online, go to dcsoky.gov and use Pay Taxes Online. Several bills can share a cart, the options are card or electronic check, and the fee appears before you confirm. The office warns that payments sent through any other website will not be honored.

  • At the counter: cash, card, check, cashier's check or money order, with checks for the exact amount
  • By mail: checks payable to the Daviess County Sheriff's Office, drawn on U.S. banks only
  • Online: card or e-check on the sheriff's own site

Two bills for one parcel usually mean an exemption was added after the first printing. Read both and look up the balance online. If the amounts differ, ask the tax counter which one reflects the exemption before you pay, so you don't pay twice or miss a discount window.

sections.h2: How do I challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
Start by phoning the PVA at 270-685-8474. No appeal is allowed without a conference with the PVA or a deputy, and that has to occur during the thirteen-day May inspection window that begins the first Monday of May. What's being tested is fair cash value as of January 1.

When the conference settles nothing, file at the County Clerk's office, 270-685-8434, by the close of the following workday. The local board of assessment appeals sits 25 to 35 days after the window ends and rules on evidence, so bring comparable sales, an appraisal or repair quotes. A board ruling you dispute can go to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

People at least 65, or classified as totally disabled, can claim it on the home they occupy. For 2025 and 2026 it is worth $49,100 off the assessed value.

The application goes to the Daviess County PVA. A driver's license, birth certificate or passport proves age. A disability claim needs proof that a federal agency or a retirement system classified you as totally disabled.

If you sold or bought after January 1 and think a bill came in error, the sheriff's office suggests asking the closing title company. Valuation fixes on January 1 under KRS 132.220, so paperwork can trail a sale. Your settlement statement should split the year's tax between seller and buyer.

A delinquent notice is sent on February 11. When business closes on April 25, unpaid bills pass to the County Clerk, carrying heavy fees and exposure to the tax sale. A delinquency can be paid off from the sale proceeds at closing.

Practical steps: ask the sheriff's counter for the balance on each parcel, ask whether an exemption was added or removed this year, and make sure the buyer's lender has a copy of the bill that was actually printed.

Some sellers short on time choose a straight as-is cash sale. The buyer takes the house without repairs, and the tax balance, whether current or delinquent, is paid from the proceeds at closing. That suits an inherited or vacant house. Even so, get every balance in writing first and check that it shows as its own line on the closing statement.

sections.h2: What a delinquent bill turns into
sections.html:
After April 25 the bill becomes a certificate of delinquency held by the County Clerk, with a lien on the parcel. The state process adds interest at 1 percent a month, a 10 percent clerk fee and a 20 percent county attorney fee. The county attorney mails notices by mid-May and mid-June, and installments may be possible.

From mid-July to late October the clerk may sell certificates to private buyers, after advertising the list in the local paper and on the clerk's website at least 30 days ahead. Once a buyer holds the certificate, the owner pays that buyer, who adds charges. Settle a delinquency before the summer sale dates if you plan to sell. The clerk's phone is 270-685-8434.

faqs.q: When does the Daviess County 2 percent discount end?
faqs.a: December 10 every year. The window opens November 10, and bills are mailed in the first week of November.

faqs.q: What is the final day to pay a Daviess County bill before it goes to the clerk?
faqs.a: April 25, at close of business. After that the bill moves to the County Clerk with added fees and can be offered at the tax sale.

faqs.q: Can I pay Daviess County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Pay Taxes Online link on the Daviess County Sheriff's Office site, dcsoky.gov. Card and e-check payments carry a fee that shows before you confirm.

faqs.q: Who do I phone when my Daviess County value looks too high?
faqs.a: The PVA at 270-685-8474, to book the conference that Kentucky requires before an appeal can be filed with the County Clerk.

faqs.q: Does Owensboro bill its own property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Owensboro Tax Office, 270-687-8537, bills city tax separately from the county bill the sheriff sends.
